problem_text:
A logistics company must dispatch a specialized technician to perform maintenance at eight distinct facilities across a region.  
The geographical positions of these facilities are recorded as follows:  

Facility Alpha: Coordinates (98,2)  
Facility Beta: Coordinates (25,100)  
Facility Gamma: Coordinates (142,132)  
Facility Delta: Coordinates (74,114)  
Facility Epsilon: Coordinates (125,149)  
Facility Zeta: Coordinates (182,173)  
Facility Theta: Coordinates (55,108)  
Facility Iota: Coordinates (21,94)  

Travel distances between facilities, measured in kilometers, have been precomputed:  

Alpha to Gamma: 137.2 km  
Alpha to Delta: 114.5 km  
Alpha to Epsilon: 149.5 km  
Alpha to Zeta: 190.5 km  
Alpha to Theta: 114.4 km  
Alpha to Iota: 120.0 km  
Beta to Gamma: 121.3 km  
Beta to Delta: 51.0 km  
Beta to Epsilon: 111.4 km  
Beta to Zeta: 173.1 km  
Beta to Theta: 31.0 km  
Beta to Iota: 7.2 km  
Gamma to Delta: 70.3 km  
Gamma to Epsilon: 24.0 km  
Gamma to Zeta: 57.3 km  
Gamma to Theta: 90.2 km  
Gamma to Iota: 126.8 km  
Delta to Epsilon: 61.9 km  
Delta to Zeta: 123.1 km  
Delta to Theta: 19.9 km  
Delta to Iota: 56.6 km  
Epsilon to Zeta: 61.8 km  
Epsilon to Theta: 81.1 km  
Epsilon to Iota: 117.6 km  
Zeta to Theta: 142.7 km  
Zeta to Iota: 179.3 km  
Theta to Iota: 36.8 km  

Due to regulatory restrictions, no direct travel link exists between Facility Alpha and Facility Beta.  
Moreover, the routing plan must incorporate exactly one of two specific mandatory connections: either the link between Beta and Gamma, or the link between Gamma and Delta.  

The objective is to determine the minimal total travel circuit that visits every facility precisely once and returns to the point of origin.
